messages.author: 839dfa09184985a5
messages.subject: Installing RStan and Question about Instructions
parts:
I'm trying to install RStan and Mavericks and I'm getting this error over and over:

Warning: unable to access index for repository http://wiki.rstan-repo.googlecode.com/git/src/contrib/rstan_2.2.0.tar.gz/src/contrib

trying URL 'http://wiki.rstan-repo.googlecode.com/git/src/contrib/rstan_2.3.0.tar.gz'

Error in download.file(url, destfile, method, mode = "wb", ...) : 

  cannot open URL 'http://wiki.rstan-repo.googlecode.com/git/src/contrib/rstan_2.3.0.tar.gz'

In addition: Warning message:

In download.file(url, destfile, method, mode = "wb", ...) :

  cannot open: HTTP status was '403 Forbidden'

Warning in download.packages(pkgs, destdir = tmpd, available = available,  :

  download of package ‘rstan’ failed


Also, with regards to the instructions online, it says that ~/.R/Makevars should have the following text:

CXX=g++ -arch x86_64 -ftemplate-depth-256 -stdlib=libstdc++
but that doesn't match
if (!file.exists("~/.R/Makevars")) {
  cat('CXX=g++ -arch x86_64 -ftemplate-depth-256 -stdlib=libstdc++\n
       CXXFLAGS="-mtune=native  -O3 -Wall -pedantic -Wconversion"\n', 
       file="~/.R/Makevars");
} else {
   file.show("~/.R/Makevars");
}

On Tue, Jun 24, 2014 at 10:54 AM, Peter Li <li.pe...@gmail.com> wrote:
I'm trying to install RStan and Mavericks and I'm getting this error over and over:

Warning: unable to access index for repository http://wiki.rstan-repo.googlecode.com/git/src/contrib/rstan_2.2.0.tar.gz/src/contrib

trying URL 'http://wiki.rstan-repo.googlecode.com/git/src/contrib/rstan_2.3.0.tar.gz'

Error in download.file(url, destfile, method, mode = "wb", ...) : 

  cannot open URL 'http://wiki.rstan-repo.googlecode.com/git/src/contrib/rstan_2.3.0.tar.gz'

In addition: Warning message:

In download.file(url, destfile, method, mode = "wb", ...) :

  cannot open: HTTP status was '403 Forbidden'

Warning in download.packages(pkgs, destdir = tmpd, available = available,  :

  download of package ‘rstan’ failed
I updated the wiki page with a new repo yesterday.  I am not sure why it seems that you saw a previous version of this page.  Try to refresh the webpage?

Also, with regards to the instructions online, it says that ~/.R/Makevars should have the following text:

CXX=g++ -arch x86_64 -ftemplate-depth-256 -stdlib=libstdc++
but that doesn't match
if (!file.exists("~/.R/Makevars")) {
  cat('CXX=g++ -arch x86_64 -ftemplate-depth-256 -stdlib=libstdc++\n
       CXXFLAGS="-mtune=native  -O3 -Wall -pedantic -Wconversion"\n', 
       file="~/.R/Makevars");
} else {
   file.show("~/.R/Makevars");
}

If you are using xcode 5.1, you can leave all of those alone as it is for 5.0.1.  In 5.1, the default template depth is 256 and we don't need -stdlib=libstdc++.  So maybe you don't need to mess with ~/.R/Makevars at all for the most recent xcode. 
 
--

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Installing RStan and Question about Instructions
parts:
On Tuesday, June 24, 2014 11:34:29 AM UTC-4, Jiqiang Guo wrote:
Then put CXX = clang++ in your ~/.R/Makevars 

What version of R are you using?  I wonder the newest version of R for Mavericks (R-3.1.0-mavericks.pkg) has set CXX to clang++ instead of llvm-g++.

For R 3.1, we can force clang++ on Macs by setting CXX_STD = CXX11 in Makevars. I think we should be discouraging llvm-g++-4.2 because it does not compile models anyway.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Installing RStan and Question about Instructions
parts:
Nice! Smoothest RStan install yet! Thanks so much for making
this easier, Ben. Let's hope it works as easily for Andrew --- he's
our bellwether for install problems.

I particularly appreciated:

1. Much leaner and cleaner and more automated instructions (I
didn't get lost once), and

2. not having to stop and start R or uninstall/install
RStan manually. (I didn't even glance at the script --- that's
how trusting us dumb users are).

What didn't work is an install from the terminal. See Attempt 1.
Attempt 2 is from the GUI, and that worked just fine.

Attempt 1 (from the terminal)

The first thing it does is pop up a modal dialogue box
saying "To open "R," you need to install X11", which pops
open this web page when I say "continue" on the dialog box:

http://support.apple.com/kb/HT5293?viewlocale=en_US&locale=en_US

(reading the fine print of which leads me to some sourceforge
like thing for Mac).

It then conveniently exits R with no warning. WTF?


Attempt 2.

I then went and read the Mac OS instructions, which had me install
the new R first, 3.1.0. That worked just fine without even shutting
down the R GUI.

I started with Xcode 5.1.1 installed.

There's no more Step 3 on the Mac OS instructions --- can you change
that to just point back to the cross-platform instructions if that
was the intent?

It indeed asked for a CRAN mirror and proceeded to install a new
Rcpp.

The -j4 worked brilliantly!

Awesome!

- Bob
